rationale:
Evidence: the best raced design is iteration 2 (score 65.2489): sensors at x = ±0.024, kp 7.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.4, last_direction. All 60 trials ended off track with no finishes. Max error is 0.0677 (oval), 0.0614 (s-bend) and 0.0645 (slalom), so every track exceeds the 0.06 m limit. rms error is 0.024 to 0.028 m, so the failures are peak excursions. Line losses run 1 to 2 per run. Across iterations 0 to 2, max_error on the oval moved only between 0.064 and 0.068 while the gains changed, so the gains are not the main limit on peaks. The sensing span is the main untested lever.

Review of the round-2 critique. I accept point 1: widening the sensors to x = ±0.06 cuts the near-centre slope of the steering signal by about 2.5 times, which acts like a much lower kp and confounds the sensor test. I accept point 4 and the kill-rule concern, since coarser signal may raise oscillation for reasons unrelated to edge coverage. I accept point 5: the sensors at ±0.06 cover offsets 0.044 to 0.060 m only in the outer band, so the benefit is real but narrow. I reject the critique's suggestion to add a kp rescale (kp about 13 to 16). That would also multiply turn authority at the edges by about 2 times, which is a second large change with its own oscillation risk. I also reject returning to the raced layout, since no test would then be learned.

Change: sensor x set to ±0.045 with inner sensors at ±0.0225 and centre at 0 (positions -0.045, -0.0225, 0, 0.0225, 0.045; y = 0.05). Under the engagement rule (about 0.02 m beyond each sensor's x), the outer sensors see tape to roughly 0.065 m offset, which covers the 0.044 to 0.060 m band the current layout misses. The near-centre slope falls by about 0.53 times rather than 0.4 times, so the confound is halved. Gains are kept at the best-raced values (kp 7.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.4, last_direction). I do not change ki, kd or speed, because the critique gives no evidence that ki 0.2 helped (iteration 3 scored lower at 65.0106), and completion is not reachable without a separate speed test.

Hypotheses: max_error falls below 0.0614 m on the oval and slalom; line_loss_events fall to 1 or fewer per run; oval progress rises above 0.25. The result is not expected to finish any run. Kill rule: if steering_oscillation rises by more than 30 percent, or max_error does not fall on at least two tracks, the next race returns to x = ±0.024 and tests kp alone. If runs stay on track with completion_time above 3 s, base_speed rises by 0.1 in a single-change test.
